Think of a decision your company, school, town or family made five years ago. How would things be different now if it had decided otherwise?
exercicios.frase: If they hadn't
exercicios.resposta: Five years ago, my town built a market near the bus station. If they hadn't done that, the sellers would still be on the main road. But there's no parking. If the town had more money, they'd have built a car park too.

exercicios.enunciado: Is it useful to think about "what would have happened if…", or is it a waste of time? Why?
exercicios.frase: would
exercicios.resposta: It's useful if you learn something. If I hadn't thought about my mistakes, I'd make the same ones today. But if you think about it too much, you'd never decide anything new.

exercicios.frase: Had it not been for Kalandula, Tômbwa would never have happened.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com o acento em "Had" no início.
You are presenting to a board. Explain one past decision and one possible future decision, using at least three inversions (Had we…, Should…, Were we to…, Had it not been for…).
exercicios.frase: Had
exercicios.resposta: Two years ago we moved our servers to the cloud. Had we not done so, last year's flood would have stopped us for weeks. Were we to open on Saturdays, we would need two more staff. Should the committee approve, we could start in June.

exercicios.enunciado: Does formal language make a proposal more convincing, or does it put people off? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: A little formality helps, because it shows you've prepared. But too much puts people off. One elegant sentence at the key moment is more convincing than a whole speech in legal English.

exercicios.frase: [Given] that Kalandula pays half, it's the cheapest option for us.

Nesse caso, revemos o preço de seis em seis meses.
exercicios.resposta: In which case, we review the price every six months.

exercicios.frase: I'm Rajesh. Windhoek costs five hundred thousand, the whole budget. One point two million, provided we win one tender in five.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Windhoek's most likely result depend on?

exercicios.frase: This is Rajesh. In Nampula, Mussiro would be seventy percent of the revenue.
exercicios.enunciado: What percentage of the Nampula revenue would come from Mussiro?

exercicios.frase: The contracts should be in dollars. Otherwise, the currency eats the profit.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com uma pausa antes de "otherwise".
Explain a plan as a chain: one fact (given that), one assumption (assuming), one condition (provided that), and what you'll do if things go wrong (in which case, otherwise).
exercicios.frase: in which case
exercicios.resposta: Given that I already cook for three offices, I have clients. Assuming they stay, I'll start with two days a week, provided the rent stays low. Prices may go up, in which case I'll cook at home. I need a licence by June; otherwise I can't sell to companies.

exercicios.enunciado: When you make an important decision, do you think more about the best case or about the worst case? Why?
exercicios.frase: worst case
exercicios.resposta: I think more about the worst case, because if I can survive the worst case, the decision is safe enough. The best case is nice to imagine, but it rarely happens.

licoes.objectivo: Comparar cenários com graus de certeza e de risco.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: In the [best]-case scenario, we win two tenders out of five.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: The most likely [outcome] is one and a half million.

"It's a calculated risk." This sounds…
"On balance, Luanda." The speaker means…
"The upside is a stable currency." The upside is…
Ponderando tudo, Luanda é a melhor opção.
exercicios.resposta: On balance, Luanda is the best option.

exercicios.frase: I'm Lindiwe. In the best-case scenario, we win two tenders out of five. Two million in year three.
exercicios.enunciado: What is the best case for Windhoek?

exercicios.frase: This is Rajesh. Even the worst case in Luanda is better than the most likely outcome in Windhoek.
exercicios.enunciado: What is Rajesh's point?

opcoes.texto: Luanda's worst case beats Windhoek's most likely case.

exercicios.frase: I'm Inês. If Mussiro left us, we'd drop to six hundred thousand.
exercicios.enunciado: What would happen in Nampula if Mussiro left?

opcoes.texto: Revenue would drop to six hundred thousand.

exercicios.frase: Luanda is cheaper, but Windhoek is safer.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com o acento em "cheaper" e "safer".
Compare two or three options for a real decision. For each, give the best case, the worst case and the most likely outcome. Then say which calculated risk you'd take, on balance.
exercicios.frase: On balance
exercicios.resposta: I'm choosing between a job in Benguela and staying in Luanda. In the best case, I'd be a manager in two years; in the worst, the new office closes. Staying is nowhere near as exciting. On balance, Benguela is a calculated risk I'd take.

exercicios.enunciado: Should a company always present more than one option to its board, even when the team already knows what it wants? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: Yes, because the board needs to see that the team looked at everything. If you show only one option, it looks like you're hiding the others.

exercicios.frase: strategy, strategic; economy, economic; diversify, diversification.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita: o acento muda de sílaba.
Advise a company that wants to grow: where to gain a foothold, whether to diversify, how to reduce exposure to risk, and when it would break even.
exercicios.frase: foothold
exercicios.resposta: My recommendation is a long-term strategy in two steps. First, gain a foothold in Huambo with one small shop, and break even in the first year. Then scale up. I wouldn't diversify yet: it would increase our exposure to risk.

exercicios.enunciado: Should a company stay out of politics, or does it need to understand politics to make good strategy? Why?
exercicios.frase: politics
exercicios.resposta: A company should stay out of party politics, but it must understand politics and government policy. If you don't know what the government intends to do, your strategy is just a guess.

licoes.objectivo: Seguir uma discussão de estratégia a quatro vozes e identificar posições e interesses.

exercicios.frase: I'm Zodwa Ngcobo. Twelve million rand for growth. Option one, four new shops. Option two, online delivery. My recommendation is online.
exercicios.enunciado: How much money does Seringa Fresh have for growth?

exercicios.frase: This is Zodwa. Forty percent of our customers already order online, from our competitors.
exercicios.enunciado: What percentage of customers already order online from competitors?

exercicios.frase: I'm Ravi Pillay. Online needs no new buildings, so it would break even in about two years. Four shops, five or six years.
exercicios.enunciado: How long would online take to break even?

exercicios.frase: I'm Karen Holt. I represent the fund that owns thirty percent of this company.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Karen's fund own?

exercicios.frase: This is Karen Holt. Simon, with the greatest respect, you're seventy-two. Who leads this company in five years?
exercicios.enunciado: What is Karen's real question?

opcoes.texto: who will lead the company in five years

exercicios.frase: I'm Simon Ngcobo. Fine. A test. Six months. Durban only.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Simon finally accept?
What is really behind Simon's position?

opcoes.texto: the fear of losing control of the company he built

exercicios.enunciado: Zodwa answers: "Had we never listened to a new idea, we'd still have one shop." She is…

opcoes.texto: using her father's own structure against him

exercicios.frase: Had we never listened to a new idea, we'd still have one shop.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita em voz alta.

exercicios.frase: Should you choose online, we'd want to see a test first.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita em voz alta.
You are a consultant who watched the meeting. Tell Zodwa privately what each person really wants, and give her one piece of strategic advice.
exercicios.frase: really
exercicios.resposta: Your father isn't really against online; he's afraid of losing what he built. Ravi wants profit, and Karen wants to know who leads after your father. My advice: make the Durban test work, and give your father a role in it.

exercicios.enunciado: Is it a good idea for family businesses to bring in outside investors? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: Often yes, because an outsider asks the questions the family avoids, like who leads next. The downside is that the family loses some control.

Present three options for a decision you know: the upside, the risk and a number for each; recommend one; and answer "What if your main assumption is wrong?". Use one mixed conditional and one inversion.
exercicios.frase: Were it not
exercicios.resposta: Our school can buy a library, computers or solar panels. Had we had solar panels last year, we wouldn't have lost thirty days to power cuts. I recommend solar. What if the cuts stop? We'd still save on diesel. Were it not for the batteries' cost, it would be obvious.

exercicios.enunciado: Present these data in English, in three sentences, including one risk: "Restauração em Benguela, 2030: 35% dos restaurantes abriram nos últimos três anos; 58% dos clientes querem entregas ao domicílio; renda média no centro: 450 000 Kz por mês; principal risco: falta de pessoal qualificado."
exercicios.frase: risk
exercicios.resposta: The market in Benguela is growing: about a third of restaurants opened in the last three years, and more than half of customers want home delivery. Rent in the centre is about four hundred and fifty thousand kwanzas a month. The main risk is finding qualified staff.
exercicios.contexto: Mediação: o essencial, com um risco.

exercicios.enunciado: Think of a decision your company, school or town made five years ago. How would things be different now if it had decided otherwise?
exercicios.frase: would
exercicios.resposta: Five years ago, my company chose a cheaper supplier. If it hadn't, we wouldn't have so many complaints today. Had we spent a little more then, we'd be saving money now. Should it happen again, I'd ask for a test first.

exercicios.enunciado: A director asks: "What if your main assumption is wrong?" Answer about a plan of yours, with in which case or otherwise.
exercicios.frase: in which case
exercicios.resposta: My main assumption is that our clients will stay. They might not, in which case we'd still have the new website to find others. And we'll review it after six months; otherwise we could lose a whole year.
